Compression is used to reduce the file size of video in order to share it or send it to others. Lossy compression is a type of compression in which file sizes are typically smaller, but quality is lost. MP4 is an example of Lossy Compression type. Lossless Compression is a type of compression in which quality is not lost. This results in very high quality and large file sizes which require large data storage capacity for video. Many high-end video cameras can shoot raw lossless video but the file sizes are extremely large and normally require post processing. Answers could include: Lossy Codecs use algorithms to compress the video by removing still pixels and reducing the colour depth of the video to save data storage. Interlaced video is a compression technique for doubling the perceived frame rate of a video display without consuming extra bandwidth. The interlaced signal contains two fields of a video frame captured at two different times. This enhances motion perception for the viewer, and reduces flicker by taking advantage of the phi phenomenon.

Before incorporating pre-existing components into a multimedia presentation, it is crucial for a project team to address ethical and legal concerns. Ethically, they should consider issues related to intellectual property rights, ensuring they have the appropriate permissions or licenses to use third-party content. This involves respecting copyright laws and adhering to fair use guidelines when applicable which can potentially prevent reputational damage. Legally, the team must assess potential liabilities regarding any copyrighted material or trademarks they intend to include. This includes verifying that their usage complies with relevant copyright laws, licenses, and agreements. Moreover, they should be cautious about any potential defamation or privacy issues that might arise from using certain content. Answers could include: Give proper attribution • If you use components that are protected by copyright, you must give proper credit to the creator or owner of the material. This includes the name of the creator and the source of the material. Be mindful of trademark law • If you use trademarks or logos in your multimedia presentation, you should also make sure that you are not violating trademark law. This may include obtaining permission from the trademark owner or ensuring that the use of the trademark is considered ‘fair use’. Protect the privacy rights of individuals • If you use images or videos of individuals in your presentation, make sure you have obtained their consent or that the use of their image is protected by law. Section III

Organisation A, a partnership-owned firm w ith a hierarchical structure, tends to have a formal approach to marketing and advertising. This means that decisions about how t o promote their products or services go through different levels of management before being put into action. Each partner might have a say in these decisions, which can take time. They may have specialised teams for different marketing tasks, like research or branding. In contrast, Organisation B, a sole trader-owned firm w ith a flat management structure, takes a more flexible approach. This means that decisions about marketing are made more quickly because there are fewer levels of management. A sm all team m ight handle marketing directly, allowing for faster reactions to changes in market conditions.

• Decision-making speed – Hierarchical structures (Organisation A) may experience slower decision-making due to the various levels of approval required. – Flat structures (Organisation B) typically allow for quicker decisions due to fewer layers of management. • Responsiveness to change – Organisation A might be less responsive to change because of its many tiers of management, which can slow down the implementation of new ideas. – Organisation B is likely more agile and can adapt quickly due to its simpler structure. • Quality control – In a hierarchical structure, quality control can be more standardised and rigorous, although potentially slower. – Flat structures might have more flexible quality control processes, allowing for quicker adjustments but possibly less consistency. • Resource allocation – Hierarchical firms may have more complex resource allocation processes, potentially leading to inefficiencies. – Flat structures might allocate resources more dynamically and efficiently due to less bureaucracy. • Innovation • Communication • Employee autonomy • Management overhead • Cost efficiency • Risk management. 2024 HSC Industrial Technology Multimedia Technologies The multimedia industry has been significantly affected by various historical developments in manufacturing processes. During the late 20th century, the introduction of digital technology revolutionised the production and distribution of multimedia content. This shift from analogue to digital allowed for higher quality production, easier editing and faster distribution. In the 21st century, advancements in microprocessor technology have further transformed the industry. These developments have led to the creation of more powerful and compact devices, such as smartphones and tablets, which have become primary tools for consuming multimedia content. The miniaturisation of components has also allowed for the integration of multiple functions into single devices, enhancing user experience. The rise of cloud computing has had a profound impact on the multimedia industry as well. Cloud technology enables the storage and streaming of vast amounts of content, making it easily accessible to users worldwide. This has led to the growth of streaming services like Netflix and Spotify, which have revolutionised how m ultimedia content is consumed and distributed. These historical advancements have collectively enhanced the efficiency, accessibility and quality of multimedia production and distribution. They have also opened up new possi bilities for innovation and creativity, shaping the industry into what it is today.
